overview.headline: Constant velocity flight and range from ground speed times time

keyPoints.point: An airplane maintains constant speed level flight when lift equals weight and thrust equals drag
keyPoints.quote: an airplane can maintain a constant speed and level flight, in which the lift is equal to the weight, and the thrust is equal to the drag.

keyPoints.point: Ground speed remains constant while wind speed stays constant enabling distance calculation
keyPoints.quote: The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.

keyPoints.point: Distance flown equals ground speed multiplied by time aloft expressed as d equals V times t
keyPoints.quote: the distance flown is equal to the ground speed times the time aloft.

keyPoints.point: Maximum distance aircraft can fly equals ground speed times maximum time known as maximum range
keyPoints.quote: The maximum distance that the aircraft can fly is then equal to the ground speed times the maximum time (tmax).

keyTerms.gloss: aircraft speed relative to ground that remains constant when wind speed is steady
keyTerms.quote: The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.

keyTerms.gloss: greatest distance aircraft can fly limited by maximum time and fuel load
keyTerms.quote: We call this distance the maximum range (R) of the aircraft.

keyTerms.gloss: steady velocity maintained when lift equals weight and thrust equals drag
keyTerms.quote: an airplane can maintain a constant speed and level flight, in which the lift is equal to the weight, and the thrust is equal to the drag.

keyTerms.gloss: half of total range used for round trip military missions
keyTerms.quote: The combat radius would be half of the range as specified here.

keyTerms.gloss: maximum time aloft determined by fuel load before engine stops
keyTerms.quote: The maximum distance that the aircraft can fly is then equal to the ground speed times the maximum time (tmax).
